speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The combination of weakness, decreased sensation, burning pain, and significant weight loss in the right arm raises concern for a structural lesion or malignancy. Have you noticed any visible swelling, skin changes, or lumps in your right arm or shoulder area?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine and Shoulder.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results are normal, but given the pain, sensory changes, and weight loss, I need to know if this started after a specific injury or if you have any history of cancer.

REQUEST TEST: Tumor Markers (CEA, CA 15-3, CA 19-9).
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine.
Have you experienced any night sweats or fevers recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal lab results rule out common metabolic deficiencies or acute infections, but the significant weight loss and burning pain are highly concerning for an underlying malignancy or chronic inflammatory process. Have you noticed any night sweats, fevers, or unintentional weight loss in the past three months?

REQUEST TEST: Tumor Markers (CEA, CA 15-3, CA 19-9).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated CEA and CA 15-3 tumor markers are highly suggestive of breast cancer, even though the MRI of the cervical spine is currently normal. Did you have a previous diagnosis of breast cancer, or do you notice a lump, skin dimpling, or discharge from your nipples?

REQUEST TEST: Bilateral Mammography and Breast Ultrasound.
REQUEST IMAGES: Bilateral Mammography.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The latest imaging reports normal readings for the breast ultrasound and mammography, despite your elevated tumor markers. To further characterize the potential malignancy causing your arm symptoms, have you noticed any new lumps, skin dimpling, or nipple discharge in your breasts?

REQUEST TEST: Bone Scan (whole body).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal mammography and ultrasound are puzzling given the elevated CEA and CA 15-3 markers. Since the initial symptoms involve the right arm, could there be a primary breast cancer with metastasis to the brachial plexus or bone that wasn't picked up on the initial imaging, or perhaps an axillary recurrence?

REQUEST TEST: Bone Scan (whole body) and PET/CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Breast Cancer (Axillary recurrence or distant metastasis to brachial plexus/bone causing radiculopathy).
